headline: Long-read pipelines are benchmarked against orthogonal truth sets across DNA, RNA and signal-level tasks
label: Long Read Benchmarking And Calibration
summary: New benchmarks test long-read assembly, RNA diagnosis and m6A calling against short-read or GLORI references, tying performance to data type and filtering.
synthesis: The common thread is empirical calibration of long-read analyses against reference or orthogonal data. A preprint compares five local-assembly consensus strategies for structural variant calling on simulated and real HiFi and ONT data, with data-type-dependent results. The eLife study benchmarks Dorado versions for direct-RNA m6A calling against GLORI and proposes stringent filtering. A Genome Medicine study compares PacBio Kinnex RNA-seq with short-read RNA-seq in 50 individuals with Mendelian disorders. Workflow papers add evaluation on synthetic truth data (MitoArc, short-read mtDNA with NUMT-aware assessment) and nanopore-based HIV-1 resistance profiling (NanoHIV-DR). HARICOT and GapCNV extend methods, assembling raw nanopore signals without basecalling and detecting CNVs in low-input DNA respectively. The items are heterogeneous; the dominant emphasis is on validated, data-type-aware performance.
